ground_truth:
FINAL CONFIRMED DIAGNOSIS: Familial Hemiplegic Migraine Type 2 (FHM2) — a rare autosomal-dominant monogenic migraine syndrome presenting here as a stroke mimic with prolonged hemiplegic aura, encephalopathy, seizures, and fever.

HOW CONFIRMED: Whole-exome sequencing identified a heterozygous pathogenic mutation in the ATP1A2 gene (encoding the alpha-2 subunit of the astrocytic Na+/K+-ATPase). The diagnosis was further supported by the constellation of negative alternatives: non-contrast CT showed no hemorrhage/territorial infarct; MRI showed CORTICAL diffusion restriction crossing the right parietal and temporal cortices in a NON-vascular (non-arterial-territory) distribution; CT angiography suggested an M1 cut-off but digital subtraction angiography demonstrated a PATENT vessel with reversible VASOSPASM and NO thromboembolism; LP showed acellular CSF with normal protein/glucose and no viral DNA; EEG showed diffuse 1-3 Hz delta slowing (severe encephalopathy) without true seizure focus; autoimmune/paraneoplastic antibody panels negative.

CORRECT DISPOSITION/TREATMENT: Recognition that this is NOT an ischemic stroke or infectious/autoimmune encephalitis. Stop unnecessary thrombolytic/antiplatelet-for-stroke and empiric antiviral pathways once mimics excluded. Ground truth: confirmed diagnosis is Familial Hemiplegic Migraine Type 2 (FHM2), confirmed by whole-exome sequencing showing a heterozygous pathogenic ATP1A2 mutation; treatment was oral nimodipine (calcium-channel blockade) plus levetiracetam for seizures; MELAS/mitochondrial disease was NOT the answer. Note the derived rulebook itself ranks mitochondrial stroke-like episode (MELAS) as top and demotes hemiplegic migraine — i.e., the engine's most-likely verdict DIVERGES from the true confirmed diagnosis. So the test is whether each output lands on the true diagnosis, not whether it faithfully reflects the engine.

OUTPUT A — leads with hemiplegic migraine ("most likely sporadic or familial hemiplegic migraine") as the unifying diagnosis at moderate confidence (~60-65%). This MATCHES the ground truth. Specific hits: explicitly names familial hemiplegic migraine and the gene panel CACNA1A/ATP1A2/SCN1A — ATP1A2 is the actual confirmed gene; notes ATP1A2 attacks can include fever and coma (directly on point for this fulminant presentation); recommends sending the hemiplegic-migraine genetic panel (matches the real confirmatory pathway — genetic testing); recommends a calcium-channel blocker, verapamil/nimodipine (matches the actual treatment, nimodipine); correctly excludes infection/autoimmune, stops aspirin, avoids tPA/thrombectomy, continues levetiracetam.
